text.content: Circle Nurture feature list v1.8-12-26
Circle Nurture — what it will do
Here is everything Circle Nurture will do, in everyday words. Review it and tell me if it matches what you meant — confirm it as-is or tell me what to change.
Your people, in one private place.
Add the people who matter — family, friends, coworkers, mentors — without turning it into a data-entry job. Just a name and whatever small detail you want to remember about them.
Circles.
Put people into circles — "Family," "College friends," "Work," your book club. A person can be in more than one. Circles are just how you group the people you care about; they're never group chats.
Memories, jotted down.
A date, a small moment, a detail — "got the promotion," "loves sourdough," "kids are 4 and 6." Kept on your phone, private to you.
A calm home screen.
Your people, your circles, at a glance. It should feel human, not like a spreadsheet.
Message one person.
One tap and your phone's own text messenger opens, ready to send to that person — from your number, like any normal text.
Blast a message to a group — privately.
Write one message, pick the people (or a whole circle), and each person gets it as their own private one-to-one text. Nobody sees who else got it. Replies come back to you privately.
A gentle nudge, never homework.
When it's been a while since you reached out to someone who matters, the app quietly notices. No scorekeeping, no guilt — just "hey, it's been a bit."
The right words, when you want them (TrueTone).
You tell it what you mean to say; it drafts a few versions in your own voice. You always read and approve the exact words before anything is sent. It never writes to your people on its own.
The story of your year.
A way to look back and see the connections you kept alive and the memories you gathered — the piece you'd actually show somebody.
The privacy core underneath all of it
Your people, your memories, your messages stay on your phone. This is a private tool, not a social network.
The MVP — the first version you'll hold
Per your done-condition, the first version is the first three items in action: add people, jot a memory, send a blast message. Everything else builds on that.
Once you confirm this list (as-is or with changes), I'll write the full specification for the overnight build.
